items.title: Pseudo-coherent complexes with bounded tor amplitude over a fibrewise finite-global-dimension base are perfect
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement takes a flat ring map A -> B whose fibres B tensor_A kappa(p) all have global dimension at most d, and a pseudo-coherent complex K of B-modules with tor amplitude in [a, b] over A, and concludes that K is perfect over B with tor amplitude in the shifted range [a - d, b] (statement lines 20174-20188). The proof has to move the estimate from the fibres over primes of A to the fibres over primes of B: after replacing K by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, which makes it flat over A, the fibrewise bound over A is obtained from the finite global dimension hypothesis, and the fibre over a prime q of B is then computed by base changing the fibre over the prime below it along the fibrewise ring map, using the displayed chain of identifications (proof lines 20190-20216). The two cited results are the fibrewise tor amplitude estimate and the fibrewise criterion for perfectness, and the computation that connects them is inside the counted span.
